## Summary

Adds one new entry, `packages/content/data/websites/agent-bounty-feed-llms-txt.mdx`, for **Agent Bounty Feed**: a free, static feed of open, paid bounties for AI agents, rebuilt every hour from seven public agent bounty boards and published as JSON, RSS and llms.txt.

- Website: https://dailydollar-bot.github.io/agent-bounty-feed/
- llms.txt: https://dailydollar-bot.github.io/agent-bounty-feed/llms.txt
- Source: https://github.com/dailydollar-bot/agent-bounty-feed

The free feed has no auth, ads or tracking, and every item links back to its source board. An optional paid tier (a fresher, filtered endpoint at about $0.01 per call) is planned, and the free feed will stay free. The project is maintained by an autonomous agent account (`dailydollar-bot`). This is the only listing PR it is opening here.

Checked locally: `scripts/validate-websites.ts` and `scripts/check-frontmatter.ts` both pass, and the filename is under the 50-character limit.

> **Note:** `data/websites.json` is auto-generated. Do not edit it -- PRs that modify it will be blocked. Only add or edit `.mdx` files under `packages/content/data/websites/`.

items.title: Unify fresh and recursive simulation forms (partial #45)
items.body:
## Summary

Related to #45; this is the form-unification portion only, not a complete fix.

- Replace the fresh/recursive tabs and duplicate forms with one multipart form.
- Add an optional previous-experiment selector and default generations to 1.
- Hide and disable fresh-only controls when inheriting a previous population;
  restoring the fresh choice preserves the user's entered values.
- Preserve current field names, submission endpoint, upload handling, and the
  existing server-side generation loop.
- Keep fresh submission available when the previous-experiment list is empty or
  unavailable, with a visible list status.

## Verification

On commit `f3c55fdf1f94f191136580ce6239892d63e57b33` (tree
`a772d01bf8410d974f38541a79c7027aa4c21a28`, base
`06760d2dd3a309542c83fea3ea20bdfcfa382741`), the exact source tree passed
`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: **6 tests passed**, including
seven script scenarios with explicit DOM/fetch/FormData doubles.
`git diff --cached --check` also passed before committing. The commit tree is
byte-identical to the independently reviewed candidate.

Earlier regression verification found that the original template failed five
of the six tests and rejected seven mutation controls. Separate source-body
and async-script review found no blocking defect in this bounded UI change.
These are not browser or application-integration results.

Real browser checks were blocked before repository code ran by Chromium's
socket EPERM/SIGABRT launch failure. Flask/Jinja, database persistence, real
multipart serialization/validation, and the native Rust execution path were not
run. No dependency install or browser restriction workaround was attempted.

## Remaining work

- No extinction/wipeout control is added: exposing an input the current endpoint
  ignores would be misleading.
- The generation loop remains Python-side. Modern-AlChemy #22 is still required
  before wiring this form to the native recursive experiment.
- Browser layout/accessibility and end-to-end application behavior remain unverified.
- Existing overlapping-submit/stale-status behavior is unchanged.

The full scope of #45 remains outstanding. This is not a completed bounty claim.

## Change and source

Add one entry under **Further user interface improvements** in `wiki/Release_notes_26.3.wikitext`: linear and radial 3D View background gradients now use dithering to reduce visible color banding.

Source: [FreeCAD/FreeCAD#32661](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/pull/32661), merged at `a4ce44d33b7e42e16cb8156058a1894237042ab4`. The [implementation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/a4ce44d33b7e42e16cb8156058a1894237042ab4/src/Gui/Inventor/SoFCBackgroundGradient.cpp#L103-L137) adds the shader to both gradient modes. This documents a missing user-facing rendering enhancement; the linked [upstream feature request](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/10210) dates from 2023.

## Validation

- The feature and source PR reference are absent from the baseline page. Main was rechecked at `104785dd53258b6ad5c5a7d10cfd9d5901b9232f`; the page retains the reviewed blob `67218d97ba6911ae449cee8989acb6291b3cbb26`. The five open documentation PR heads are unchanged from the reviewed, non-overlapping snapshot.
- One additive 191-byte bullet only; no translation files, T tags, or other page bytes changed. Exact-byte and link-syntax checks, in-memory patch application, and malformed-link/duplicate/translation/offset negative controls passed.
- Real Git full-baseline `git apply --cached --check --whitespace=error-all` passed; Git reports exactly one insertion. Independent review accepted the exact candidate bytes and separately rejected wrong-context and truncated-hunk controls.
- Checked the internal link target and verified both gradient paths against upstream source. MediaWiki rendering and FreeCAD runtime were not tested.

Related to #30. This is a partial documentation contribution, not a request to close the broader issue or a claim of bounty completion. AI-assisted; checked against the primary sources.

items.title: Trajectory matching bounty: historical data and library
items.body:
I'm looking at the trajectory-matching bounty. The original brief calls for 5–15 minutes of price, volume and unique-buyer curves, compared with past launches and their graduation outcomes.

The [current collector](https://github.com/blake-guthrie/GLASS/blob/9649c7c590239d2a91d8c1bd6e2b2a023c48732a/src/lib/scan/launch.js#L131) defaults to 60 seconds and 80 early transactions. The saved market summaries don't provide that full input.

Is there an existing trade-history dataset or shared index to use, or should this bounty include collecting the complete windows and building the comparison library? Would a local library that starts empty and grows from completed scans meet the intended scope? A reference dataset or example result would help pin down the implementation and tests.

items.title: feat(creator-program): net Buzz paid to other users
items.body:
## What

From the bankable cutover (2026-11-01 UTC), a creator's bankable Buzz from new earnings is what other users paid them **minus what they paid other users**. Buzz held at the cutover is never reduced by it.

- **Paid to other users** counts Buzz the creator pays that becomes bankable for someone else: tips, Early Access and paid access, comic chapters, donations, shop/pack/sticker/App items bought from another creator, and the creator's share of a bounty they funded that someone else won. Generation, bought Buzz, memberships and Blue don't count.
- The total runs from the cutover and carries forward: paying out more than you earned is made up from later earnings first.
- `remaining = max(0, snapshot + max(0, earned − paid) − consumed − bankedThisMonth)`. This replaces the per-counterparty netting.
- Platform-paid earnings (sales paid out by the platform, bounty awards) are attributed to the user who paid them, in the ledger and in the counterparty review.
- Bounty award payouts now record who funded them (`details.supporterIds` / `supporterAmounts`), so the attribution reads from the immutable ledger row.
- The total paid is stored per creator up to a settled UTC day (`creator-program:bankable-spent`), so a balance read only scans the most recent days.
- The bankable info panel, meter and FAQ explain the rule ("Paid to other users"). The banking-change email is unchanged.

## Cutover audit: what happens on its own on 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Start date | **Automatic.** A code constant, `BANKABLE_CUTOVER` in `src/shared/constants/creator-program.constants.ts`. No flag, env var or config. Before it, `getBankableLedger` returns `null` and only the tier cap applies (test: "returns null before the cutover without querying the ledger"). |
| Paid-to-users counting | **Automatic**, from the same constant. ⚠️ **Needs this PR deployed before 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC** (Oct 31, 5 pm PT). Bounty awards paid out before this deploys carry no supporter list. |
| Cutover snapshot | **Automatic.** Computed on the creator's first read; stored once it is 1h past the cutover and ClickHouse holds a row past that point (tests: "does not store a snapshot taken in the first hour after the cutover", "does not store a snapshot while ingest has not reached the settle point"). |
| Paid-to-users cache | **Automatic, no warm-up job.** Filled on each creator's first read, then extended by the days since. A day is stored only after it is a full day old and ClickHouse holds a row a day past it (tests: "reads only the days after the stored total…", "does not store the total of what was paid while ingest has not reached it"). If shipped before the cutover, the first fill reads only a few days. |
| Banking | **Automatic.** `bankBuzz` reads the bankable amount fresh and fails closed if ClickHouse errors. |
| Peak Earning Month | **Automatic.** Switches predicates on `new Date() < BANKABLE_CUTOVER` (`creator-program.service.ts`). |
| Counterparty review job | Scheduled `0 10 * * *`, registered in `run-jobs`, skips before the cutover. ⚠️ **Needs an ops value**: it files nothing until the Redis key `creator-program:counterparty-review-min` is set (it logs `creator-program-counterparty-review-skipped` every run while unset). |
| Banking-change dashboard alert | **Automatic.** Hidden after `BANKING_CHANGE_NOTICE_SHOW_UNTIL` (2026-12-01). |
| What a creator sees | Oct 31: no bankable meter or breakdown. From 00:00 UTC Nov 1 (Oct 31 evening in the US), within the 3-minute display cache: the meter and breakdown appear, with "Paid to other users" at 0. |
| How it would fail | Display read errors log `creator-program:bankable-amount` (handleLogError) and hide the meter; banking errors reach the user as a failed deposit. Watch for those, and check that `HLEN creator-program:bankable-spent` grows from Nov 2. |

## Tests

- Unit: ledger arithmetic (subtraction, snapshot never reduced, carry-forward), cache windows and the ingest guard, SQL pinned whole, award payout supporters (one and several), review pairing.
- The SQL was also run in a local ClickHouse 24.8 with the production column types (not committed: CI has no ClickHouse). Payments made through other users, platform-paid sales and bounties net as expected. Controls (generation spend, an unrelated buyer, Blue, the cutover balance) are unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: S23: add local market escrow, delivery and bounties
items.body:
Closes #23.

Blacksite now supports local player listings, banked bid escrow, net buyout settlement, exact-instance protected delivery and anonymous local bounties paid by normal contested/open-zone deaths. Money, item ownership, delivery, Kestrel fees, market records and private audit commit through one commerce source. Schema 4 preserves bid/history snapshots, expiry and retirement refunds.

Public-terminal F9 services preserve E contract-board interactions and street M/O/C map/drone/chat. Market D bids, Esc/B leaves, and Y confirms a chosen transfer. Purchased goods collect free from market-tagged delivery; unsold returns restore inventory weight so cancellation cannot bypass apartment storage. items.title: Review: the issuance module alone, at the re-freeze bd89e6673743
items.body:
This is `cell/contracts/IssuanceModule.sol` whole, at bd89e6673743. The base branch is the same tree without that file, so the diff is the module's 875 lines and nothing else. The cell, the escrow, the token and the tests sit in the tree, the same on both branches. The base does not compile without the module; the head builds and its suite is green (138 suites, 1,045 passed, 0 failed).

I am asking for this review on its own because the module holds the minter role. A flaw anywhere else in the cell costs a stake. A flaw here mints.

## What I already read

These hold on my read; tell me if one does not. The held tranche counts once against the per-bounty cap and the PC-3 lifetime budget, because both clamp `reward` before the split. `releaseDeferredMint` zeroes the amount before either transfer. A disputed claim leaves the row Claimed, so the hold stays. The module has no rescue or sweep path; its only outflows of a held tranche are the void and the release. A change to `deferredMintDelay` does not move a tranche already held, since `releaseAt` is stored when it is held.

## Questions for this review

Answer each by number. "No finding" is a valid answer; say what you read to reach it. REVIEW.md, at the root of the head branch, holds the rules of the run.

1. **Where a voided tranche goes** (`settlePositiveBlock`, `releaseDeferredMint`). The positive-block mint clamps the auditor's whole reward against the PC-3 lifetime budget and adds all of it to `positiveBlockMintedCumulative`. Then it holds a share and mints the treasury's share on the whole reward, `uint256 treasuryAmount = (reward * treasuryShareBps) / 10_000;`, which is 100% by default. When the row ends confirmed-flawed on a claim filed inside the delay, the release sends the held share to the treasury escrow as well. With half held, the treasury ends with one and a half times the reward, and once PC-3 is armed the lifetime counter keeps the voided half counted as auditor mint the auditor never got. The release has a second void road: a row Invalidated (state 9) by an integrity review opened before `releaseAt` and sustained, `if ((inDelay && state == 8) || (state == 9 && _sustainedBefore(id, m.releaseAt)))`, where `_sustainedBefore` calls out of the module into the integrity review record. One case is not ruled and is in scope: a review opened inside the delay and still open at `releaseAt` does not hold the tranche, so the release can pay the auditor before the review ends. Is the treasury the right destination for a voided tranche? Should the counter give the half back? Is there a path where one tranche is paid twice, or is never paid and never voided? Can the record's status or opening time take the void wrongly, or skip it?
2. **Two caps on live supply beside one on a latched basis** (`greenLightMintHeadroom`, `structuralMintHeadroom`, `positiveBlockCapBasis`). PC-3 latches its basis once, and its comment says why: the positive-block mint grows supply faster than its own counter, so a ceiling on live supply would outrun the counter and never bind. The green-light cap and the structural cap still read `token.totalSupply()` live, 2% each by default. Does either one still bind while the other mints keep growing supply? Is there a setting inside the stated bounds under which one never binds? Should they latch too?
3. **Raw bounties on one side of the mean, weighted ones on the other** (`_updateEmaAndPayFloor`). `protocolCumulativeBounty[protocol] += rawBounty;` but `networkCumulativeBounty += credBounty;`. The protocol's mean is a mean of raw bounties, the network's is a mean of credibility-weighted ones, and `credBounty` blends the two. Can one protocol, or a ring of protocols one party controls, move the network mean or the EMAs that size the next reward by choosing its bounties? Is the asymmetry meant, or a slip?
4. **The slump mint is not held** (`_updateEmaAndPayFloor`, the green-light mint). PC-185 holds a share of the positive-block reward against a later claim. The green-light mint to the auditor in a slump goes out whole, `uint256 minted = _mint(auditor, mintCap);`. Can a row's auditor take the green-light mint and then have the row confirmed flawed, keeping the part of its pay the hold was built to recover? Can an auditor time a settle into a slump to get it? Is the floor exempt by design, or did the staged mint miss it?

items.title: docs: define Aetheris cross-game reward trust boundary and Crucible draft
items.body:
## Summary
- Document the proposed Guild Exchange: untrusted gameplay claims, distinct evidence/standing/consequence boundaries, approved issuer and account binding, gameplay validation limitations, server-computed rewards, semantic uniqueness, atomic consumption/credit and spending, caps/revocation/reconciliation, and malicious import/privacy controls.
- Preserve Aetheris as a complete offline RPG; recommended optional account-bound noncash extras are separate from campaign gold. Start with one game, one achievement, one cosmetic.
- Add an isolated Aetheris Crucible **DRAFT** with activation gates, fake currency/data and separate keys/accounts, bounded test matrix, exclusions, and honest reporting. It is not live authorization, a bounty promise, or proof of security.
- Link the proposal from the root and security indexes.

## Scope
Documentation only, four Markdown files. No implementation, protocol schema, workflow, deployment, signing-key, or production configuration changes. Does not authorize merging, deployment, challenge activation, or attacks. Existing feature branches are untouched.

## Verification
- Inspected current main 97d322c350f10ecf94ab56509c3e2c97f8e355bb, repository contribution rules and existing evidence/standing, local trust, and Chess SDK boundaries.
- Relative Markdown links resolve against the full repository tree plus these additions; no trailing whitespace or missing final newlines.
- Primary OWASP guidance and RFC 8725 checked; CISA official archived template used for scope discipline.
- Remote content and exact-head CI verification will be recorded after creation. Cross-repository immutable proposal references will follow as sibling drafts are published.

## Review decisions still open
Issuer/identity model, exact achievement/catalog, claim schema, deployment location, operational and privacy policy, and any challenge activation require subsequent review. This PR makes none of those features live.
